question: Should ordered startup configuration layers become a supported OpenClaw core CLI and lifecycle contract while the managed-configuration RFC remains open?
rationale: The implementation defect has a mechanical repair, but accepting a new public configuration ownership model requires maintainer intent that code review cannot infer.

options.title: Wait for RFC approval
options.body: Keep the draft open, repair path scoping, and land only after the RFC confirms the supported core contract.

options.title: Keep composition external
options.body: Use a host launcher or existing startup snapshot seam if maintainers do not want core to own ordered layers.

options.title: Sponsor the feature now
options.body: Approve the public mode now and require explicit ownership, compatibility, and lifecycle proof before merge.

recommendation.title: Wait for RFC approval
recommendation.body: Keep the draft open, repair path scoping, and land only after the RFC confirms the supported core contract.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision concerns a broad core Gateway/config product contract rather than only a local implementation detail.
